name: George W. Bush

summary.text: George W. Bush, later the 43rd President of the United States, ran the Texas oil company Spectrum 7 until Harken Energy acquired it in September 1986, after which he served as a Harken director (1986 to October 1993), a paid consultant (from April 1987) and, per PBS, an audit committee member. In 1989 he bought a stake in the Texas Rangers baseball partnership using a $500,000 bank loan. On June 22, 1990 he sold 212,140 Harken shares for about $848,560 and disclosed the sale to the SEC roughly eight months late; the SEC investigated from April 1991 and closed the inquiry in October 1993 without enforcement action, stating that the termination was not an exoneration. His Rangers stake, bought for $606,302, returned $14.9 million when the team was sold in 1998. This record covers only his business roles that the site's pages reference.

facts.claim: Bush joined Harken Energy's board of directors when Harken bought his company Spectrum 7 in a stock swap announced on September 22, 1986. He served as a Harken director from 1986 until he resigned effective October 26, 1993, and as a consultant to Harken from April 1987 under a contract reported at $80,000 a year, raised to $120,000 in 1989.
facts.quote: Bush resigned from Harken's Board of Directors effective October 26, 1993 and terminated the Consulting Agreement under which he had served as a consultant to Harken since April 1987.

facts.claim: PBS reported that in the Spectrum 7 deal Bush received about 212,000 Harken shares, a consulting arrangement, and a seat on Harken's board and its audit committee.
facts.quote: he received about 212,000 shares, a consulting deal, and a seat on the board and audit committee

sources.title: President Bush's Old Business at Harken Energy Corporation

facts.claim: Bush took two loans from Harken totaling $180,375, in 1986 and 1988, to buy Harken stock, according to SEC filings cited by the Washington Post; they carried 5 percent interest, reported as below the prevailing market rate, and he later retired the debt by surrendering 105,000 shares held as collateral. In July 2002 the White House called the loans entirely appropriate and fully disclosed.
facts.quote: Bush accepted loans totaling $180,375 from Harken Energy Corp. in 1986 and 1988, according to Securities and Exchange Commission filings.

sources.title: Bush Took Oil Firm's Loans as Director
Bush Took Sweetheart Loans

facts.claim: On June 22, 1990, Bush sold all 212,140 of his Harken shares at $4 a share, about $848,560 gross (the Post reported $835,307 net on his notice of proposed sale), weeks before Harken reported a second-quarter loss of about $23 million on August 20, 1990. Bush said he sold to pay off the $500,000 bank loan he took in 1989 to buy his Texas Rangers stake.
facts.quote: Bush's sale of all of his 212,140 shares of Harken stock for $4 a share on June 22, 1990, just before the conclusion of a second quarter that produced huge losses.

sources.title: Bush Name Helps Fuel Oil Dealings

facts.claim: Bush filed the Form 144 notice of proposed sale on the day of the June 1990 sale but did not file the Form 4 disclosing the completed sale until about eight months later (the Washington Post reported 34 weeks). The SEC's inquiry found that he had filed late Form 4s for Harken transactions on four occasions, involving stock worth more than $1 million. Bush blamed the delay on the SEC, saying it had lost the filing.
facts.quote: The Post reported that Bush disclosed the transaction 34 weeks late, and the SEC discovered he had disclosed sales of Harken stock late for four transactions totaling $1 million.

facts.claim: The SEC opened its investigation of Bush's Harken sale on April 5, 1991, the day after the Wall Street Journal reported his late filing. Staff memos of August 21, 1991 and March 18, 1992 concluded there was insufficient evidence for an insider trading case; the Center for Public Integrity's summary of the SEC records says investigators concluded that neither Bush nor Harken's leadership were aware of the magnitude of the loss when he sold, and that the SEC never interviewed Bush.
facts.quote: According to SEC documents, investigators concluded that neither Bush nor the rest of the company's hierarchy were aware of the magnitude of the loss at the time Bush sold his stock.

sources.title: A brief history of Bush, Harken and the SEC
Securities and Exchange Commission documents

facts.claim: On October 18, 1993, the SEC wrote that the investigation had been terminated as to the conduct of Mr. Bush and that no enforcement action was contemplated with respect to him, adding that the termination must in no way be construed as indicating that the party has been exonerated or that no action may ultimately result from the investigation.
facts.quote: the investigation has been terminated as to the conduct of Mr. Bush, and that, at this time, no enforcement action is contemplated with respect to him

facts.claim: In October 1994 Bush said of the Harken inquiry: 'The SEC fully investigated the stock deal. I was exonerated.'
facts.quote: "The SEC fully investigated the stock deal," he said in October 1994. "I was exonerated."

sources.title: Right on the money: The George W. Bush profile

facts.claim: A week before his June 1990 sale, Harken's outside lawyers cautioned Bush and other directors against selling shares if they had significant negative information about the company's prospects, the Washington Post reported in November 2002; Bush had said he obtained clearance from Harken general counsel Larry Cummings to sell. The Washington Post also reported in 1999 that Bush warned fellow directors against Harken's Bahrain project at board meetings.
facts.quote: Bush had said earlier that he got clearance by the lawyer [Harken general counsel Larry E. Cummings] to sell this stock.

facts.claim: Bush invested $606,302 in the 1989 purchase of the Texas Rangers, of which $500,000 was a bank loan; his stake grew from 1.8 to 11.8 percent before the team was sold in 1998, and his share of the sale proceeds was $14.9 million, which he reported as 1998 income.
facts.quote: his cut from the proceeds of the sale was $14.9 million, a 25-fold return on his investment of $606,302

openQuestions: No source found in this session documents any payment to Bush from a UAE account or from BCCI or its shareholders. The money Bush received in the Harken period came from Harken itself (stock, options, consulting fees and two company loans) and from his 1990 stock sale on the open market; the Boston Globe reported that Harvard Management did not buy his shares, and the buyer of the 212,140 shares is not identified in any source found.
The site's node says the Rangers investment 'later yielded a $15M windfall'; the Center for Public Integrity figure is $14.9 million.
Bush's audit committee membership rests on PBS NewsHour and Center for Public Integrity reporting; the Harken proxy statements on EDGAR would confirm it.
